w10_P4_000004: A drop-test rig in a car-seat laboratory fires a sled of 45000 grams along a straight horizontal rail. The rig's control sheet states that the sled's release speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. Each launch, the data logger records the energy the sled carries because of its motion at release. The rig makes 4 launches in a burst, runs 5 bursts in a test block, and completes 9 test blocks in one shift, and the logger simply adds up every launch. At the end of the shift the software subtracts a fixed instrument offset of 19 J from the accumulated total. The rail is 12 m long, a figure the logger never uses. What total, in joules, does the logger report at the end of the shift?
w10_P4_000005: A quality laboratory publishes a final figure that is 4 times the number it obtains after subtracting a calibration allowance of 20 J from the day's raw total. That raw total is 11 times the energy delivered by a single shot of a pneumatic ram whose moving head has a mass of 4 kg. The muzzle speed of that head, in metres per second, is exactly 2 times the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 12x + 35 = 0. The ram is bolted 0.9 m above the bench, a height that has no bearing on the energy of the shot. What is the published final figure, in joules?
w10_P4_000017: A magnetic launcher accelerates a carriage of 55000 grams from rest along a level track. Measured from the instant of release at t = 0 seconds, the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 1t^2 + 6t, and the launcher drives it this way for the first 3 seconds. At the end of that run the logger records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion. Each test consists of 5 identical carriage runs whose recorded energies are summed, after which the logger adds a standing offset of 19 J to the test total. The facility completes 9 such tests and adds their figures together, and the same 9-test programme is then repeated at 5 separate sites, with all site totals combined. The track is 40 m long, which plays no part in the accounting. What is the combined figure, in joules?
w10_P4_000026: A flywheel test cell spins up a rotor rim segment whose mass is 52000 grams and then releases it along a guide. The release speed of the segment, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 15x + 56 = 0. The instrumentation records the energy the segment carries because of its motion, and then expresses that record in kilojoules. The cell fires 5 segments in each run, performs 3 runs per rotor, and tests 4 rotors in the campaign, with every recorded figure added together. A safety shield 2 m from the guide is noted in the log but is irrelevant to the energy. What is the campaign total, in kilojoules?
w10_P4_000027: A conveyor audit reports a headline number that is 7 times the figure obtained for a full week. That weekly figure is 11 times the daily figure, the daily figure is 10 times the figure for one hour, and the hourly figure is 9 times the force needed for a single push. In each push a trolley of 132000 grams is driven forward, and the trolley's acceleration during the push, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0. The pusher itself is driven by a motor mounted at the far end of the line. What is the headline number, in newtons?
w10_P4_000028: A rehabilitation gym uses a sled that pushes an athlete of 83 kg horizontally on a frictionless air track. During the push the athlete's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 11x + 28 = 0. The machine's load cell records the force required for one push, and the daily report multiplies that reading by 9 because the programme calls for 9 pushes. From that daily figure the software subtracts a tare of 6 N, then converts the result to kilonewtons. Finally, a fixed contractual credit of 27 kN is subtracted from the converted value to give the number entered in the ledger. What number, in kilonewtons, is entered in the ledger?
w10_P4_000038: A vibration bench carries 7 identical sensors, and the calibration routine works through every distinct pair of sensors that can be chosen from them. The number of such pairs is, in metres per second squared, the acceleration the bench imposes on a test mass of 149000 grams during the sweep. The controller records the force needed to drive that mass and adds a fixed preload of 30 N to the reading. It then multiplies the result by 3 for the three axes, by 10 for the ten sweeps in a session, and by 3 again for the three sessions in the certification. The bench frame is 1.5 m wide, a dimension that never enters the calculation. What is the certification figure, in newtons?
w10_P4_000040: A test rover of 35000 grams runs along a straight rail, and its position in metres at time t seconds is modelled by the fitted curve x^3 + 6x^2 with x standing for t. Engineers need the rover's speed at the instant t = 3 seconds, which is the rate at which that fitted position is changing there. From that speed they compute the energy the rover carries because of its motion, and they express the result in kilojoules. A standing allowance of 30 kJ is then added for the drive electronics, and the whole figure is multiplied by 10 because the rail carries 10 rovers running identically. The rail's guard fence stands 3 m to one side and has no role here. What is the final figure, in kilojoules?
w10_P4_000041: A press-shop report ends with a value expressed in kilonewtons, obtained by multiplying an earlier figure by 4 for the four presses on the line. That earlier figure was itself 3 times a shift figure, and the shift figure was 7 times the force acting on a single ram. The ram has a mass of 169 kg, and its acceleration builds during the stroke: the rate at which the acceleration grows, in metres per second cubed, follows 1t^2 + 5t, and between t = 3 seconds and t = 4 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval. The ram's guide column is 2 m tall, which does not enter the force calculation. What value, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000042: A machine-shop ledger closes by adding a fixed handling allowance of 10 kN to a figure that is 6 times an earlier converted reading. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of a value obtained by adding a preload of 23 N to the force on a single tool head. The tool head has a mass of 163 kg, and its position along the slide in metres is fitted by the curve 5x^3 - 5x^2, with x the time in seconds. Its acceleration at the moment x = 2 seconds is the rate at which the slope of that fitted position curve is itself changing there. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the ledger?
w10_P4_000045: A warehouse tug accelerates a loaded pallet of 120 kg along a smooth floor. The pallet's acceleration during the pull, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0. The tug's controller records the force needed for one pull and multiplies it by 7, because the shift calls for 7 identical pulls. It then subtracts a rope-tension tare of 26 N from that total and converts what remains to kilonewtons. The pallet is stacked 1.8 m high, a figure the controller records but never uses. What is the converted result, in kilonewtons?
w10_P4_000048: A packing plant has 325 red cartons and 176 blue cartons, and the supervisor forms the largest possible number of identical bundles that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. The number of cartons that then goes into each bundle is, in metres per second squared, exactly 7 times that number of bundles, and this is the acceleration the plant's shuttle applies to a tray of 47000 grams. The control system records the force needed to drive the tray and multiplies it by 5 for the five shuttles on the floor. The result is expressed in kilonewtons and then multiplied by 5 again, once for each working day of the week. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the control system report for the week?
w10_P4_000050: A linear actuator drives a carriage of 147000 grams along a rail, and its speed in metres per second is modelled by the fitted curve 4x^3 + 5x^2, with x the elapsed time in seconds. The carriage's acceleration at the instant x = 1 second is the rate at which that fitted speed is changing there. The controller computes the force needed to produce that acceleration and expresses it in kilonewtons. It then multiplies the converted value by 10, because 10 carriages run on the rail, and by 9, because 9 rails share the same drive cabinet. The cabinet is 2 m from the nearest rail, a distance with no bearing on the force. What is the reported figure, in kilonewtons?
w10_P4_000057: A materials laboratory files a certificate whose number is 7 times a monthly figure. That monthly figure is 5 times a weekly figure, and the weekly figure is 7 times the energy of a single shot expressed in kilojoules. In one shot a striker of 33 kg is accelerated from rest along a horizontal guide, and its acceleration in metres per second squared follows 3t^2 + 0t between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, where t is the time since release. The energy the striker carries because of its motion at the end of that interval is what the shot record holds, before it is expressed in kilojoules. What number, in kilojoules, appears on the certificate?
w10_P4_000058: A haulage ledger records a number obtained by subtracting a contractual credit of 24 kN from a converted figure. That converted figure is the kilonewton form of a value found by taking a daily total and subtracting a coupling tare of 28 N. The daily total is 3 times the force needed for one launch of a shunting cradle whose mass is 140 kg. During a launch the cradle's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0. What number, in kilonewtons, goes into the ledger?
w10_P4_000059: An air-track glider of 34000 grams is released and slides freely along a level rail. Its speed on release, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0. A demonstration consists of 10 identical releases, and the class adds up the energy each glider carries because of its motion. That summed figure is then expressed in kilojoules, and the lecture is repeated for 10 separate classes, with all the figures added together. What total, in kilojoules, does the department record?
w10_P4_000072: A drone workshop fits the curve 2x^3 + 5x^2 to the trace from a test flight, with x the elapsed seconds. At the moment x = 3 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a payload of 9000 grams released at that instant. The workshop records the energy the payload carries because of its motion, and multiplies it by 9 because 9 payloads are released on every flight. From that flight total it subtracts a telemetry allowance of 23 J, expresses the remainder in kilojoules, and adds a fixed ground-station allowance of 18 kJ. The drone's rotors span 1.2 m, which has no part in any of this. What is the final recorded value, in kilojoules?
w10_P4_000075: A depot receives 369 steel bars on one truck and 328 on another, and the foreman splits both loads into identical stacks using the largest stack size that divides both counts exactly. He then removes 15 bars from one such stack, and the number remaining is, in metres per second squared, the acceleration his hoist gives to a test load of 139000 grams. The hoist's cell records the force needed to accelerate that load, and the reading is expressed in kilonewtons. A fixed rigging allowance of 25 kN is then added to give the number written on the certificate. What number, in kilonewtons, is written on the certificate?
w10_P4_000078: A test report ends by adding a fixed handling allowance of 30 kJ to a figure that is 12 times the energy of a single impact expressed in kilojoules. That impact is made by a hammer of 26 kg swinging freely into a target. The hammer's speed at contact, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0, and the energy of the impact is the energy the hammer carries because of its motion at that instant. The hammer hangs from a pivot 2 m above the target, a length the report notes but does not use. What number, in kilojoules, ends the report?
w10_P4_000081: A launcher accelerates a sled of 51000 grams from rest along a level track, and its acceleration in metres per second squared follows 3t^2 + 5t between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, with t measured from release. At the end of that interval the logger records the energy the sled carries because of its motion and expresses it in kilojoules. A fixed instrument offset of 24 kJ is added to the converted value, and the sum is multiplied by 7 because the programme calls for 7 identical launches. From that programme total a calibration credit of 23 kJ is subtracted to give the certified number. The track's guard rail is 30 m long and plays no part. What is the certified number, in kilojoules?
w10_P4_000082: A ballistics summary ends with a value that is 12 times a monthly figure, and that monthly figure is 9 times a weekly figure. The weekly figure is what you get by adding a fixed range allowance of 5 kJ to the energy of one shot expressed in kilojoules. In that shot a projectile of 25 kg leaves the tube, and its muzzle speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0. The energy of the shot is the energy the projectile carries because of its motion as it leaves the tube. What value, in kilojoules, ends the summary?
w10_P4_000083: A baggage conveyor brings a case of 13000 grams up to speed in 4 equal stages, and every stage adds 4 metres per second from the drive roller plus a further 2 metres per second from the tensioner. The terminal logs the energy the case carries because of its motion once all the stages are complete. Because a full trolley carries 5 identical cases, the logged figure is multiplied by 5, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. A standing allowance of 13 kJ for the drive cabinet is then added, and a further allowance of 27 kJ for the sorter is added after that. The conveyor is 60 m long, a figure that never enters the energy account. What is the terminal's final figure, in kilojoules?
w10_P4_000090: A robotic gantry accelerates a carriage of 165000 grams along its beam, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is 5 times the sum of 7 and 6. The controller records the force needed to drive the carriage and adds a bearing preload of 2 N to that reading. It multiplies the sum by 4, because the gantry carries 4 identical carriages, and then subtracts a frame tare of 25 N from the machine total. Finally the figure is multiplied by 8 for the 8 gantries in the hall. The hall's beam sits 5 m above the floor, a height that has no bearing on the forces. What is the figure for the hall, in newtons?
w10_P4_000093: A crane-yard report closes with a number found by subtracting a contractual credit of 27 kN from a converted total. That converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure that is 10 times the force on a single hook, since 10 hooks work together. Each hook accelerates a block of 185 kg, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is 5 times the sum of 3 and 13. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the report?
w10_P4_000094: A pneumatic rig on a teaching bench launches a puck of 13 kg across a smooth surface. The puck's launch speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0. The bench software records the energy the puck carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. Because each demonstration fires the puck along 2 lanes, the converted figure is multiplied by 2, and because the timetable runs 11 demonstrations, that result is multiplied by 11. The bench itself is 0.9 m tall, which the software never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the software report?
